item.title: Best JavaScript Date Pickers in 2026: 5 Vanilla JS Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best JavaScript Date Pickers in 2026: 5 Vanilla JS Libraries Compared

Short answer. Choose flatpickr if you want the broadest free feature set (ranges, multiple dates, date and time, months side by side, a native input on phones) and can live with a library that has not shipped a release since April 2022. Choose Air Datepicker if you want a free, dependency-free picker that is still released (3.6.0, May 2025) and you do not need users to type dates. Choose Vanilla JS Datepicker if you need ready Bootstrap 5 styles and multiple dates for free, without time selection. Choose Web Awesome Pro if you already pay for Web Awesome and want a segmented date field. Choose CoreUI PRO if your app runs on Bootstrap and you want range presets, week to year selection and validation states that match the rest of your forms.

item.title: Best JavaScript Modal Libraries (2026): 6 Dialog Options Compared
item.description:
Best JavaScript Modal Libraries (2026): 6 Dialog Options Compared

Short answer. If you write your own CSS, start with the native <dialog> element: showModal() gives you a modal in the browser’s top layer, stacked dialogs, a non-modal mode and a cancelable close, with no library at all. Web Awesome Dialog (MIT) wraps the native element with a header, a close button, a footer slot, light dismiss and page scroll lock. Micromodal and a11y-dialog are tiny, unstyled scripts that handle opening and closing your own markup, and both support nested dialogs. If your project already uses Bootstrap, the Bootstrap modal remains the most complete styled option, with sizes, responsive fullscreen and scrollable bodies. The CoreUI modal is the same component in CoreUI’s styling: use it when your app is built on CoreUI, not as an upgrade over Bootstrap.

item.title: Best JavaScript Multi Select Libraries (2026): 7 Vanilla JS Options Compared
item.description:
Best JavaScript Multi Select Libraries (2026): 7 Vanilla JS Options Compared

Short answer. Slim Select is the most complete free multi select in plain JavaScript: tags, a “{number} selected” counter, select all for the whole list and per group, minimum and maximum selections, search, async loading and creating options, all MIT with no dependencies. Tom Select is the best pick for Bootstrap 5 projects that want a free library: checkbox options, a clear button, creating and pasting values, async loading and a Bootstrap 5 theme in the package. Choices.js is a solid MIT choice for tag-style inputs with fuzzy search. Select2 still works well for paged remote data if jQuery is on the page. CoreUI Multi Select is the most complete for selection itself (three-state select all, selecting whole groups, checkboxes, counter mode and limits) with Bootstrap styling, and it is a paid PRO component.

item.title: Best JavaScript Select and Autocomplete Libraries (2026): 7 Options Compared
item.description:
Best JavaScript Select and Autocomplete Libraries (2026): 7 Options Compared

Short answer. Tom Select is the best free all-rounder: search with custom scoring, match highlighting, creating options, async loading, loading more results on scroll, option templates and a Bootstrap 5 theme in the package, under Apache-2.0 with no jQuery. Slim Select is the lightest maintained alternative (no dependencies, released October 27, 2026) with highlighting and async search. Choices.js suits forms that need fuzzy search and creating options in a small MIT package. Select2 is back in active maintenance and strong on remote data and paging, but it still requires jQuery. CoreUI Autocomplete fits Bootstrap apps that want highlighting, inline completion hints and Bootstrap validation styles in one component, and it is a paid PRO component.

item.title: Best JavaScript Sidebar Components (2026): Vanilla JS Navigation Sidebars Compared
item.description:
Best JavaScript Sidebar Components (2026): Vanilla JS Navigation Sidebars Compared

Short answer. For a plain JavaScript or Bootstrap app, there are three realistic starting points. CoreUI Sidebar (MIT) is the most complete ready-made navigation sidebar: narrow icon mode, expand on hover, an automatic mobile overlay, nested groups, section titles, badges and a dark variant as classes and methods. Bootstrap Offcanvas is the right choice when you want a simple slide-in panel and are happy to build the navigation from Bootstrap’s Sidebars examples. Web Awesome Page (MIT) is the best full-page layout: navigation, header, aside and footer regions that turn the navigation into a drawer on phones, without navigation items of its own.

item.title: Best JavaScript Table Libraries (2026): 5 Data Tables Compared
item.description:
Best JavaScript Table Libraries (2026): 5 Data Tables Compared

The best JavaScript table library depends on how much you want built in and what your budget is. DataTables 3 is the strongest free default: since version 3 it no longer needs jQuery, and its MIT core plus free extensions cover multi-column sorting, column filters, server-side processing, row selection, pinned columns, virtual scrolling, export and an official Bootstrap 5 integration; only editing is paid. Tabulator packs the most into one free MIT package, including tree rows, inline editing with undo, resizable columns and XLSX and PDF export. Grid.js is fine for small, simple tables, but it has not released since March 2024. simple-datatables is a light option with editing and export, under LGPL-3.0 rather than MIT. CoreUI Data Grid is a commercial grid with virtualization, column filters with operators, editing and Excel export built in, sold as a separate product.

item.title: Best React Date Pickers in 2026: 10 Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best React Date Pickers in 2026: 10 Libraries Compared

Short answer. Choose Mantine if you want the broadest free feature set (ranges with presets, multiple dates, date and time, month and year pickers) in one MIT package. Choose MUI X Date Pickers if you build on Material UI and need a segmented field and time zones, knowing that the range picker is a paid Pro feature. Choose react-datepicker if you want a standalone drop-in picker with week, month, quarter and year modes and no design system attached. Choose Chakra UI or HeroUI if you need time zones and a segmented field without paying: both ship them under MIT. Choose CoreUI PRO if your app runs on Bootstrap or CoreUI and you want a range picker with presets, quarter selection and validation feedback that matches the rest of your forms.

item.title: Best React Modal and Dialog Components (2026): 10 Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best React Modal and Dialog Components (2026): 10 Libraries Compared

Mantine Modal is the most complete free React modal: stacked modals, an official manager that opens confirm dialogs from code, fullscreen, inside scrolling and documented SSR behaviour. Chakra UI Dialog matches it on API breadth, with an overlay manager, nested dialogs and a documented non-modal mode. Ant Design Modal is still the quickest way to build Modal.confirm() flows in antd apps. PrimeReact Dialog has the richest layout options (nine positions, dragging, maximize), under the PrimeUI License. For Bootstrap apps, React Bootstrap Modal and CoreUI CModal both go fullscreen below a breakpoint with a single prop, and neither supports nested modals.

item.title: Best React Multi Select Components in 2026: 9 Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best React Multi Select Components in 2026: 9 Libraries Compared

Short answer. Choose MUI Autocomplete with multiple if you are on Material UI: chips, a “+N” overflow label, a checkbox example and free-text creation, all MIT. Choose Ant Design Select in mode="multiple" if lists are long and you need a selection cap: it virtualizes by default and has maxCount and responsive maxTagCount. Choose Mantine MultiSelect if you want a dedicated free component with maxValues, pill reordering and native form submission. Choose react-select with isMulti if you need async and creatable multi selects in one familiar API and your lists are short. Choose CoreUI PRO Multi Select if you need select all, a selection limit, whole-group selection, checkboxes, a counter, virtualization, option creation and async loading documented on a single component.

item.title: Best React Select and Autocomplete Components in 2026: 9 Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best React Select and Autocomplete Components in 2026: 9 Libraries Compared

Short answer. Choose MUI Autocomplete if you are on Material UI: free text, groups, async demos, custom option and value rendering, all MIT. Choose react-select if you need a standalone searchable select with ready async (AsyncSelect) and creatable (CreatableSelect) variants and a name prop for plain form posts, as long as your option lists are not huge. Choose Ant Design Select if lists are long: virtualization is on by default. Choose HeroUI if you want built-in virtualization and a load-more pattern on React Aria foundations, for free. Choose CoreUI PRO Autocomplete if you want match highlighting, inline completion hints, async loading and virtualization as documented props on one Bootstrap-styled component.

item.title: Best React Sidebar Components (2026): 8 Navigation Sidebars Compared
item.description:
Best React Sidebar Components (2026): 8 Navigation Sidebars Compared

shadcn/ui Sidebar is the most complete free React sidebar: icon collapse, a mobile sheet, a Cmd/Ctrl+B shortcut, a state cookie, router-friendly menu buttons and RTL, as MIT code you copy into your app. CoreUI CSidebar is the strongest ready-made MIT package if you want narrow and hover-expand modes plus automatic mobile behaviour as plain props. PrimeReact 11 Sidebar matches it on modes and adds dual sidebars, under the PrimeUI License. Mantine AppShell is the best full layout system, with a navbar you can resize by mouse, touch or keyboard. Ant Design Layout.Sider with Menu is the safe pick for antd apps, especially when collapsed menus should open submenus as popups.

item.title: Best React Table Components (2026): 9 Data Tables Compared
item.description:
Best React Table Components (2026): 9 Data Tables Compared

The best React table component depends on how much you want built in. Ant Design Table is the strongest free (MIT) all-rounder: multi-column sorting, filter menus, pagination, a server-side mode, tree rows, pinned columns and row virtualization all ship in the core antd package. PrimeReact DataTable packs the most into a single component, including cell and row editing and CSV export, but version 11 moved to the PrimeUI License and has no built-in virtualization yet. TanStack Table, or the shadcn/ui recipe built on it, is the pick when you want headless logic and full control of the markup. On Mantine, mantine-datatable tracks Mantine 9, while mantine-react-table has no release for Mantine 8 or 9. CoreUI Smart Table fits Bootstrap-based CoreUI apps that need server-side sorting, filtering and pagination plus a global search box.

item.title: Best Vue Date Pickers in 2026: 8 Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best Vue Date Pickers in 2026: 8 Libraries Compared

Short answer. Choose @vuepic/vue-datepicker if you want the most complete free standalone picker: ranges, presets, multiple dates, time, all four period modes and IANA time zones in one MIT component. Choose Element Plus if you already use it: one ElDatePicker covers date, month, quarter and year ranges, shortcuts and multiple dates. Choose Vuetify if you are on Vuetify 4 and want the date field to share validation and theming with every other input. Choose PrimeVue only after reading its new license: the picker is strong, but PrimeVue 5 is no longer MIT. Choose CoreUI PRO if your Vue app is built on Bootstrap or CoreUI and you want a separate range picker with presets, quarter selection, validation feedback and documented RTL next to the rest of your components.

item.title: Best Vue Modal and Dialog Components (2026): 7 Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best Vue Modal and Dialog Components (2026): 7 Libraries Compared

PrimeVue Dialog is the most complete Vue dialog, with a confirm service, dynamic dialogs opened from code, dragging, maximizing and positions on every edge, but PrimeVue 5 is no longer MIT. Quasar QDialog is the strongest MIT choice for application flows: a dialog plugin you can call even outside components, unlimited nesting and a non-modal mode. Element Plus ElDialog is the pick when you want dragging, a before-close hook and promise-based ElMessageBox.confirm() in one MIT package. Naive UI NModal covers similar ground with useModal() and useDialog(). Vuetify VDialog and CoreUI CModal suit declarative dialogs in their own design systems, with nesting in Vuetify and one-prop responsive fullscreen in CoreUI.

item.title: Best Vue Multi Select Components in 2026: 8 Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best Vue Multi Select Components in 2026: 8 Libraries Compared

Short answer. Choose Element Plus if you want strong free defaults: collapsing tags into “+N”, multiple-limit, allow-create, remote search and a virtualized ElSelectV2. Choose Vuetify if you are on Vuetify 4: checkboxes appear next to options in multiple mode, chips are one prop away, and the list is virtualized. Choose vue-multiselect if you want a small standalone component that can select a whole group from its label and cap selections with max, for short lists. Think twice about PrimeVue MultiSelect: it has select all, a limit and a 100K-row virtual list, but PrimeVue 5 is no longer MIT and its docs mark MultiSelect as deprecated. Choose CoreUI PRO Multi Select if you need select all, a limit, whole-group selection, checkboxes, a counter, virtualization, option creation and async loading on one current component.

item.title: Best Vue Select and Autocomplete Components in 2026: 8 Libraries Compared
item.description:
Best Vue Select and Autocomplete Components in 2026: 8 Libraries Compared

Short answer. Choose Vuetify if you want the most complete free option: VAutocomplete highlights matches, VCombobox accepts free text and creates items, the list is virtualized and VSelect posts its value through a hidden input. Choose Quasar if one QSelect should do everything, including an always-virtualized list and loading more options on scroll. Choose Element Plus if you need remote search, allow-create and a separate virtualized ElSelectV2 for long lists. Choose vue-multiselect if you want a small standalone dependency with async search and tagging, for short lists. Choose CoreUI PRO Autocomplete if your Vue app runs on Bootstrap or CoreUI and you want match highlighting and Tab-accepted inline hints as documented props.

item.title: Best Vue Sidebar Components (2026): 7 Vue 3 Navigation Drawers Compared
item.description:
Best Vue Sidebar Components (2026): 7 Vue 3 Navigation Drawers Compared

Vuetify’s VNavigationDrawer is the best all-round Vue sidebar: rail mode, expand on hover, an automatic switch to a temporary overlay on small screens, vue-router support out of the box and a layout system that offsets the page for you, all under MIT. Quasar’s QDrawer is the strongest choice for mobile-first and hybrid apps, with a mini mode, swipe gestures and a visual Layout Builder. PrimeVue 5’s new Sidebar brings a modern compound API with icon mode, hover opening and dual sidebars, under the PrimeUI License. CoreUI CSidebar for Vue gives you narrow, hover-expand and automatic mobile modes as plain props in a free package. Ant Design Vue, Element Plus and Naive UI build the sidebar from a layout region plus a menu, which is the better fit when collapsed menus must open their submenus as popups.

item.title: Best Vue Table Components (2026): 7 Vue 3 Data Tables Compared
item.description:
Best Vue Table Components (2026): 7 Vue 3 Data Tables Compared

For most Vue 3 projects the answer is one of four free libraries. Vuetify is the most rounded MIT option, with separate client, server and virtualized data table components and a real mobile layout. Naive UI NDataTable has the broadest free feature list in a single component, including multi-sort, tree rows, virtual scrolling and CSV export. PrimeVue DataTable adds built-in cell and row editing, but PrimeVue 5 is licensed under the PrimeUI License rather than MIT. Quasar QTable is the natural choice inside a Quasar app, with a card-style grid mode for small screens. CoreUI Smart Table suits CoreUI and Bootstrap apps whose tables are driven by a backend API.

item.title: Bryntum Scheduler Alternatives: 8 Schedulers Compared (2026)
item.description:
Bryntum Scheduler Alternatives: 8 Schedulers Compared (2026)

Bryntum sells the most complete resource-planning toolkit on the market: Scheduler, Scheduler Pro, Calendar, Gantt, Task Board and Grid on one data model. It is also priced like a platform: per named developer, with a three-license minimum, an annual support subscription, and a separate OEM agreement if what you are building is a paid SaaS. The honest question is not “is Bryntum good?” but “do we need a planning platform, or a scheduler component?”

item.title: DayPilot Alternatives: 8 Schedulers and Calendars Compared (2026)
item.description:
DayPilot Alternatives: 8 Schedulers and Calendars Compared (2026)

DayPilot has sold scheduling components since the ASP.NET WebForms era, and its JavaScript family (Scheduler, Event Calendar, Monthly Calendar, Gantt, Kanban) is still the one many teams find first. The decision usually turns on two things: the gap between the free Lite edition and Pro is wide, with all-day events, resource columns and keyboard navigation all on the paid side; and the JavaScript edition has no built-in recurring events, which most teams discover after the first “every Tuesday” ticket.

item.title: DevExtreme DataGrid Alternatives: 8 Data Grids Compared (2026)
item.description:
DevExtreme DataGrid Alternatives: 8 Data Grids Compared (2026)

DevExtreme DataGrid is the flagship component of DevExpress’s JavaScript suite, and for classic line-of-business applications (forms, validation, master-detail, grouped totals) it is one of the most complete grids you can buy. Teams look for an alternative for three reasons that have little to do with feature count: the grid is sold only as part of a suite subscription ($899.99 per developer per year for DevExtreme Complete); the licence is not perpetual in the usual sense (after expiry you may keep the last version you received, but a licence-verification message appears in the browser console); and the grid has no cell range selection and no clipboard copy at all, which surprises every team whose users live in Excel.

item.title: FullCalendar Alternatives: 8 Schedulers and Calendars Compared (2026)
item.description:
FullCalendar Alternatives: 8 Schedulers and Calendars Compared (2026)

FullCalendar is the default answer to “we need a calendar in the app”, and for a calendar it is usually the right one. The catch appears when the calendar has to become a scheduler: the timeline view, the resource views and printing live in the Premium add-on, licensed per year. The honest question is not “is FullCalendar good?” but “are we about to pay a subscription for the three features that turn it into a scheduler?”

item.title: Handsontable Alternatives: 8 Data Grids Compared (2026)
item.description:
Handsontable Alternatives: 8 Data Grids Compared (2026)

Handsontable describes itself as “a JavaScript data grid that looks and feels like a spreadsheet”, and that sentence is the whole decision. If your users expect Excel in the browser (formulas, fill handle, merged cells, comments, pasting a range back into the sheet), Handsontable is the most complete tool for the job. If you are building a data table (render, sort, filter, edit a few cells, export), you would be paying a spreadsheet price for a spreadsheet you do not need.

item.title: MUI X Data Grid Alternatives: 8 Data Grids Compared (2026)
item.description:
MUI X Data Grid Alternatives: 8 Data Grids Compared (2026)

MUI X Data Grid is the default grid for Material UI applications, and if your app already runs on @mui/material it is usually the right first candidate. Teams look elsewhere for three concrete reasons: it is React-only, so a second framework in the company means a second vendor; the features most teams came for (more than 100 rows on screen, multi-column sorting and filtering, Excel export, clipboard paste) sit in the Pro and Premium tiers; and the licence terms around annual subscriptions, multi-app use, and developer counting deserve a careful read before procurement signs.

item.title: AG Grid Alternatives: 8 Data Grids Compared (2026)
item.description:
AG Grid Alternatives: 8 Data Grids Compared (2026)

AG Grid is the default answer to “which data grid should we use?” — and often the right one. But its most-wanted features live in a paid Enterprise tier, its bundle is substantial, and for many teams the honest question isn’t “is AG Grid good?” but “do we need this much grid?”

This comparison covers AG Grid and seven alternatives — free and commercial — on the axes that actually drive the decision: features, framework coverage, licensing cost over three years, and migration effort. CoreUI publishes this page and its own Data Grid appears below; we’ve put it where it honestly belongs, not first.

item.title: Bootstrap Alternative — CoreUI: SASS Modules + PRO Components
item.description:
CoreUI vs Bootstrap

Looking for a modern alternative to Bootstrap? Meet CoreUI – a production-ready UI toolkit that builds on Bootstrap and takes it to the next level.

🔍 What is Bootstrap?

Bootstrap is the most popular CSS framework in the world. It provides a basic set of styles and components that help developers build websites quickly.

But it comes with limitations – no official support for SASS Modules, limited JavaScript components, and no advanced templates or enterprise features.

item.title: BootstrapVue Alternative — CoreUI: Vue 3 + Bootstrap 5
item.description:
CoreUI for Vue vs BootstrapVue

Looking for a modern Bootstrap-based UI library for your Vue.js app? Here’s why developers choose CoreUI for Vue over BootstrapVue.

📦 What is BootstrapVue?

BootstrapVue was a popular UI library that brought Bootstrap 4 components to Vue 2. It offered many of Bootstrap’s features with Vue bindings.

However, the project is no longer maintained:

  • It does not support Bootstrap 5
  • It has no official roadmap or support
  • The last stable release is from early 2021
  • Vue 3 is only partially supported (via unofficial forks)

BootstrapVue was great for its time, but it’s no longer a viable choice for modern Vue.js apps.

item.title: ng-bootstrap Alternative — CoreUI: Complete UI System
item.description:
CoreUI for Angular vs ng-bootstrap

Looking for the best way to use Bootstrap with Angular? Here’s how CoreUI for Angular compares to ng-bootstrap.

📦 What is ng-bootstrap?

ng-bootstrap is a popular Angular library that reimplements Bootstrap components without relying on jQuery. It’s tightly integrated with Angular and works well with Bootstrap 5.

Its goals are clear:

  • Provide Bootstrap-style UI using native Angular components
  • Focus on quality and accessibility
  • Keep the library small and dependency-free

However:

item.title: ngx-bootstrap Alternative — CoreUI: Full Bootstrap 5
item.description:
CoreUI for Angular vs ngx-bootstrap

Need Bootstrap UI in your Angular app? Here’s a detailed comparison of CoreUI for Angular vs ngx-bootstrap.

📦 What is ngx-bootstrap?

ngx-bootstrap is a component library developed by Valor Software, designed to bring Bootstrap components into Angular. It offers wrappers for a selection of Bootstrap 3, 4, and 5 components like modals, tabs, tooltips, and date pickers.

However:

  • ✅ It partially supports Bootstrap 5, but many components (like Toasts, Spinners, Offcanvas) are missing.
  • ❌ It does not include layout systems or dashboard templates.
  • ❌ There is no commercial offering or PRO support.
  • ⚠️ Development is limited to maintaining base components — without a public roadmap or enterprise focus.

While maintained by a company, ngx-bootstrap is not a productized UI platform, and it lacks many of the features required in production-grade applications.

item.title: React-Bootstrap Alternative — CoreUI: Templates + PRO
item.description:
CoreUI for React vs React-Bootstrap

Looking for the best way to use Bootstrap in your React app? Here’s why thousands of developers and companies choose CoreUI for React over React-Bootstrap.

📦 What is React-Bootstrap?

React-Bootstrap is a popular library that reimplements Bootstrap components using native React components. It provides basic building blocks like Buttons, Modals, and Forms, staying close to the original Bootstrap spec.

However, it lacks:

  • Complex components like tables with sorting/filtering
  • Dashboard templates
  • Enterprise-ready UI elements
  • PRO features and commercial support

🚀 What is CoreUI for React?

CoreUI for React.js is a complete UI library and admin template based on Bootstrap, with hundreds of components, advanced features, and full support for modern React.

item.title: Reactstrap Alternative — CoreUI: Themes + Templates
item.description:
CoreUI for React vs Reactstrap

Looking for a Bootstrap-based UI library for your React app? Let’s compare CoreUI for React.js with Reactstrap, a long-standing open-source project based on Bootstrap.

📦 What is Reactstrap?

Reactstrap is a React component library that wraps Bootstrap 4/5 components using native React components. It offers the core set of Bootstrap elements — buttons, cards, modals, navs, etc.

However:

  • Reactstrap has no official admin templates
  • There are no advanced components (multi select, steppers, smart tables)
  • It’s maintained by volunteers, without a clear roadmap or commercial support

🚀 What is CoreUI for React?

CoreUI for React.js is a production-grade React UI library built on Bootstrap 5, with advanced components, dashboard templates, and PRO support.
